data.why: The review page only displays a results folder (counts.csv, objects.csv, overlays/) already produced by `countkit count`; it has no upload widget, so the install step runs `countkit demo` to generate synthetic plate and cell images with known counts and count them with the classic engine, giving the review page a ready results folder to open.

goals: Flip through every plate or microscope image's overlay and see which colonies or cells were counted
Click on a colony or cell the automated count missed to add it
Pick false-positive hits (dust, printed text, glare) from a list and remove them
Save corrections and get a corrected count per image without rerunning the whole batch
Check which images are flagged (crowded plate, low count, many clumps) and need a closer look

review.summary: The tree describes the CountKit review page well: moving through the batch, clicking to add missed objects, removing by number, and saving corrections, with screens that match and a clean replay. Before filing it, fix the wrong claim that the page shows no flags (the code has a flags warning box), place the triage phase where it actually happens, and fix the 'detector' wording and the overstated claim that reloading restores corrections.
